text:
Mr. president, your excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, at the outset I would like to extend my sincere congratulations to His Excellency Mr. Khalilur Rahman on his election as president of the 81st session of the General Assembly. I wish him every success in leading the work of this session. I would also like to express our deep appreciation and gratitude to the Secretary General, António Guterres, at the end of his term of office for his wise leadership in the service of peace, security, development and justice, and for his tireless efforts to preserve the standing of the organization and restore confidence in multilateral action at a time of extraordinary international complexity. When maintaining the effectiveness of the United Nations has become a demanding responsibility. And an almost daily challenge. Mr. Guterres, faced with courage and dedication, unprecedented global crises.

He leaves behind a significant legacy of committed diplomacy and principled positions. That we shall continue to remember. At this critical historical juncture for the United Nations We look forward with great hope to the selection through the process of electing the new Secretary General of the most capable and deserving individual to lead the organization with a bold, strategic vision. Building upon the efforts of his predecessor and capable of providing practical solutions for the various regions whose peoples continue to suffer the consequences of crises, wars, instability and inequality. A vision that restores hope to future generations for a better future in which the conditions for a dignified life are available to all. Mr. president we meet during this 81st session under the theme Restoring Trust and Managing Transformation a United Nations that delivers for all.

This prompts us to ask, how can we restore this trust? And before managing the desired transformation, how can we create the conditions and lay the foundations necessary for it? Our questions stem neither from doubt nor from pessimism, but from a firm conviction that restoring trust requires serious and responsible reflection on the reasons behind its decline. Tunisia's belief in multilateral action is not a product of current circumstances. Rather, it is the continuation of a journey that began before independence, when the national movement brought the cause of the Tunisian people before the United Nations and made the right to self-determination and the recovery of sovereignty, an integral part of the struggle for freedom. Following independence, Tunisia engaged fully within the United Nations to complete the foundations of its sovereignty and to build the modern state, and it succeeded in doing so.

Restoring confidence in the organization and in multilateral action requires, in our view, two essential conditions a genuine commitment and a meaningful reform process First, there must be a sincere determination and responsible commitment by all states to respect international law founded on agreement and the principle of sovereign equality among states, and to uphold the purposes and principles of the UN charter, particularly refraining from the use of force, the settlement of disputes by peaceful means and fulfilling international obligations in good faith. Second, the United Nations must embark on a comprehensive and profound reform process that responds to the transformations that have taken place in the world. This requires, in particular, reconsidering the mechanisms of decision making within the organization to ensure a more balanced and equitable geographical representation, and establishing more effective mechanisms for transparency and accountability, thus reinforcing the confidence of states and peoples in the organisation's ability to respond to the aspirations of all. Unless genuine progress is achieved on these two tracks. Collective action will remain hostage to narrow geopolitical calculations, and the gap will continue to widen between the principles we agree upon and the realities we witness on the ground. We may choose either to continue meeting under the idealism of slogans, or to commit ourselves to what can truly achieve development, prosperity and peace for all.

If we have the will, we have the capacity. Tunisia welcomes the efforts undertaken within the framework of the UN initiative. We regard these efforts as a true opportunity on which we should build, rather than a final destination in the reform process. We support the three reform tracks proposed by the initiative, provided that they are pursued through an inclusive, consultative process that preserves the intergovernmental nature of the organization and does not undermine the negotiating mandates of member states. Tunisia also believes that addressing the liquidity crisis in the organization requires all states to meet their financial obligations in full. We stress that reform should not result in a reduction of support allocated to developing countries, or to humanitarian missions and development programmes supervised by the organization and specialized agencies.

Tunisia, therefore, calls for a fair and balanced approach that safeguards both the effectiveness and credibility of the United Nations. Mr. president. Trust in the international system is measured by the extent to which its members adhere to the principles of the charter and its resolutions, and by the organisation's ability to ensure respect for international law without selectivity or double standards and to protect the oppressed peoples who have no refuge except international legitimacy How can we restore this trust? While the Palestinian people are subjected daily to the most horrific crimes and violations, and denied their most basic rights to life, security, freedom and self-determination? While the international community remains unable to put an end to their ongoing humanitarian suffering or to enforce respect for international law and international humanitarian law, my Country Tunisia condemns the continuing settlement policies of the occupying entity in the West Bank and the policies of persecution, starvation and isolation in the Gaza Strip and the the crimes of genocide that claim more lives each day. In the absence of any accountability or any punishment, Tunisia calls upon the international community to shoulder its legal, moral and humanitarian responsibilities and to end this long standing historical injustice.

Tunisia recalls that the Court of International Court of Justice in its advisory opinion of the 19th of July 2024, affirmed that the occupying entity is compelled to end its unlawful presence in the occupied Palestinian territory and that all UN member states are likewise compelled not to recognise as lawful the situation resulting from that unlawful presence. And that the United Nations, through its principal organs, should consider the means and measures required to bring that presence to an end as rapidly as possible. We further recall that the International Court of Justice and the same advisory opinion determined that the policies pursued by the occupying entity in Jerusalem form part of the process of annexation and affirmed that the domestic law of the occupying power does not alter Jerusalem's international legal status. In this context, Tunisia reiterates its categorical rejection of all unilateral measures aimed at altering the historical, legal and demographic character of holy Jerusalem, including forced displacement, house demolitions and repeated attacks on Islamic and Christian holy sites. The catastrophic humanitarian conditions endured by the Palestinian people, particularly in the Gaza Strip, as a result of continued casualties, displacement, the destruction of homes and infrastructure, and the collapse of the health care system require safe, urgent and sustained humanitarian access. It also requires allowing the UN and its specialized agencies to carry out their missions, especially the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East.

Tunisia considers that any attempt to dismantle this long standing UN agency, or to undermine its mandate prior to a just and lasting solution to the Palestinian refugee issue, constitutes a desperate attempt to eliminate the right of return and to liquidate the Palestinian cause as a whole. The logic of force may be able to impose a bitter and inhumane reality for a period of time, but it can never break the will of peoples nor halt the course of history. The will of peoples always finds its way and ultimately prevails. Such is the law of the universe and the course of history. Tunisia will remain steadfast in its support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people. Which are not subject to prescription for most among them, their right to establish an independent and fully sovereign state on the entirety of Palestine, with al-Sharif as its capital.

Mr. president, Tunisia. Tunisia follows with deep concern the continuing escalation in the Middle East and its dangerous repercussions at the security, political and economic levels. Tunisia believes that the continuation of this situation will further complicate matters and could lead to catastrophic consequences for all countries of the region and the world. Tunisia renews its call for an immediate cessation of military operations, for wisdom and reason to prevail, and for a return to dialogue and negotiations giving absolute priority to political and peaceful and diplomatic solutions as the only means of resolving existing disputes in a manner that strengthens the foundations of security and stability in the region and prevents further escalation. Tunisia also reaffirms its commitment to freedom of navigation and maritime security, in accordance with the principles and provisions of the UN convention on the law of the sea and Customary International Law, while preserving global energy security, international supply chains and the economic rights of states. Mr. president, given the bonds of brotherhood and good neighbourliness that unite the Tunisian and Libyan peoples as well as their shared, shared interests and common destiny, Tunisia supports every sincere Libyan effort and every serious UN initiative aimed at ending the crisis on the basis of a Libyan led and Libyan owned solution founded on dialogue and consensus among all parties preserving Libya's unity, sovereignty, territorial integrity and the aspirations of the brotherly Libyan people for security, stability and a unified state, Tunisia reiterates its full solidarity with the Lebanese republic and stands by the Lebanese people.

We are committed to Lebanon's sovereignty and independence, and we condemn the repeated violations of the cease fire agreement in this brotherly country in a flagrant violation of UN resolutions, Tunisia calls for the United Nations to be enabled to fully discharge its mandate in the brotherly country of Lebanon. Tunisia also condemns the repeated Zionist attacks targeting the Syrian territory and the resources of the brotherly Syrian people. We express our hope that the Syrian people will succeed in preserving the unity, independence and sovereignty of Syria over all its territory. Likewise, Tunisia follows with grave concern the continued continuing war in Sudan, and we renew our solidarity with the Sudanese people. Tunisia calls upon the United Nations to support all efforts aimed at achieving an immediate and permanent cessation of hostilities, in the hope that Sudan may restore stability and security, turn the page on conflict and focus on reconstruction and recovery. Tunisia also hopes that the Yemeni brothers will reach a comprehensive and lasting political settlement that restores security and stability to the Yemeni people and preserve the country's territorial integrity.

Tunisia renews its support for regional and international efforts to find a solution to the crisis in Yemen. Mr. president, the abundant human resources, natural wealth and promising potential of Africa make Africa an essential partner in advancing development at the international level. Yet Africa the Africa we want, continues to face intertwined security and economic challenges that require a comprehensive approach. In this regard, Tunisia reaffirms its commitment to the principle of African solutions to African problems, thereby strengthening the ownership of African countries and peoples over the resolution of their crises and reinforcing the role of African mechanisms and institutions in maintaining peace and security. Tunisia renews its support for the reform of the African Union so that it may better fulfill its responsibilities and respond effectively to current challenges. Tunisia also stresses the importance of strengthening the partnership between the United Nations and the African Union in conflict, conflict prevention, mediation, peacekeeping, peacebuilding and sustainable development.

In this context, Tunisia emphasizes its determination to continue contributing to peacekeeping efforts in Africa, a commitment it has maintained since the first years of its independence. Tunisia also reiterates its commitment to strengthen economic integration across the continent, particularly within the Common Market for eastern and southern Africa, Comesa and the African Continental Free Trade Area. Mr. president, Tunisia believes that peace, security and comprehensive development are inseparable. The essence of this session, a United Nations that delivers for all lies in the organisation's ability to serve all states and peoples according to their needs and commensurate to the challenges they face. Equality does not mean identical responses. Rather, it means ensuring that everyone benefits from the UN system while directing greater support and attention to those to those in greatest need, and to the peoples and countries facing war, poverty, marginalization and the effects of global crises.

The United Nations we seek is one that leaves no one behind, does not define need according to selective political criteria and places justice, equity, and solidarity at the core of its services to all. Guided by its firm belief in the importance of investing in people, Tunisia once again calls for a comprehensive and balanced approach to migration. That takes into account its human and historical dimensions and moves beyond a narrow security perspective while addressing its root causes. Foremost among them conflict, poverty, economic and social disparities lack of employment opportunities and development, and the proliferation of human trafficking networks. Such an approach would embody shared responsibility, solidarity and cooperation among countries of origin, transit and destination In this context, the Tunisian authorities continue their efforts to save the lives of of irregular migrants on land and at sea, provide them with care and create suitable conditions for their voluntary return to their countries of origin. In coordination with the International Organization for migration, while safeguarding their dignity and rights and combating human trafficking and migrant smuggling.

And also supporting them once they are back in their countries of origin. Tunisia once again firmly rejects becoming either a transit country or a destination for irregular migrants who are victims of human trafficking networks. Believing that climate change is a major factor affecting development, security and stability, Tunisia emphasizes that addressing this challenge requires a genuine climate justice, particularly since developing countries bear severe consequences despite their limited historical responsibility for emissions. Accordingly, countries with the greatest responsibility must fulfil their commitments regarding climate finance while maintaining a clear distinction between climate financing and development financing. Tunisia believes that achieving climate justice, comprehensive development. And pandemic preparedness and response requires reform of the international financial architecture to make it more equitable, inclusive and fair, thus ensuring developing countries have easier and fairer access to financing.

And enabling them to invest in scientific research, technology innovation and digital transformation, thereby reducing their debt burdens, strengthening their resilience and empowering them to relying on their own capacities and shaming shaping their future. My country stresses that the rapid development of artificial intelligence offers great opportunities to accelerate development goals, provided that it is accompanied by comprehensive and equitable global governance that ensure that responsible use and prevent the widening of the digital divide between north and south through capacity building, technology transfer and adequate financing. Mr. president. Under the leadership leadership of President Kais Saied, Tunisia reaffirms its unwavering determination to continue its reform process. Launched on the 25th of July 2021, with the aim of consolidating a democracy that guarantees rights and freedoms for all citizens and responds to the aspirations of the Tunisian Tunisian people for development and prosperity. My country relies primarily on its own resources and human potential, and remains committed to attracting investment, strengthening and diversifying economic partnerships based on mutual benefit, equality and mutual respect in a manner that serves its interests and preserves the independence of its decision making.

In this context context Tunisia reaffirms its steadfast commitment to human rights and public and individual freedoms in accordance with the Constitution of the 25th of July 2022, its international obligations and the choices of its people. We stressed the importance of promoting the comprehensive and interconnected nature of human rights, including economic, climate related, social, scientific, cultural and educational rights. Foremost among them the fundamental right to development. We believe that the success of reform and development depends on the participation of women and youth. Therefore, Tunisia emphasizes its commitment to strengthening the role of women in public life and in decision making positions, and to continuing efforts to combat all forms of violence and discrimination against women. Recognizing that women's empowerment is a key driver of development and stability.

Likewise, Tunisia places youth at the heart of its national priorities and works to empower them politically, economically and socially while encouraging their initiatives and their participation in public affairs and decision making. I also take this opportunity to commend all members of the Tunisian diaspora, wherever they may be, in recognition of their role in enhancing Tunisia's image abroad and supporting development efforts in their homeland. We reaffirm the president's continuous commitment to strengthening support programs for the diaspora and further consolidating ties with them So that our diaspora may continue to serve as a living example of successful integration in their countries of residence. Mr. president, Tunisia firmly believes that peace operations cannot be limited. Crisis management and conflict containment. Rather, they must contribute to creating conditions conducive to sustainable peace through supporting state institutions, the rule of law, the empowerment of local communities and enhancing development, Tunisia reaffirms its readiness to continue contributing to the development of the peacekeeping system in ways that enhance its effectiveness and credibility.

Drawing on our long standing and active participation in UN peacekeeping operations, Tunisia believes that advancing these operations requires investment in human and institutional capacities and a greater protection of civilians as a collective responsibility and humanitarian imperative. In this regard, Tunisia calls for building upon the outcomes of the international conference hosted by Tunisia in July 2025 in cooperation with the UN Department of Peace Operations on the role of armed forces and the protection of civilians, including through the establishment of an international platform for exchanging expertise and information. The development of a unified operational manual and the strengthening of training, capacity building and civil military coordination, which should include both men and women. Mr. president, in conclusion, I wish to reaffirm that the United Nations remains for Tunisia the home of international legitimacy, the House that carries the hopes and aspirations of huge future generations for a more just and equitable international order, and a unique forum. For finding practical solutions to achieve the balance of peace security and comprehensive and sustainable development. In accordance with the UN 2030 agenda.

I thank you for your kind attention. May the peace and mercy of God be upon you.

“74,000 GAZANS HAVE FALLEN VICTIM TO ISRAEL’S STATE TERRORISM”

When the Charter of the United Nations was signed on 26 June 1945, Member States declared with great hope: ‘We the peoples of the United Nations determined to save succeeding generations from the scourge of war, which twice in our lifetime has brought untold sorrow to mankind; to establish the necessary conditions under which fundamental human rights, the dignity and worth of the human, justice and respect for the obligations arising from this Charter can be maintained; to live in peace with one another with the spirit of good neighborhood; and to unite our strength to preserve international peace and security.’ More than 81 years have passed since the Charter was signed; yet humanity still yearns for the day when the powerful resolve of that time will truly come to life.

There is no need to look too far… A glance at the picture of just the past year is enough. Consider this: The past 12 months have gone down in history as one of the bloodiest periods of the last 30 years, marked by over 60 conflicts and wars. From Gaza to Ukraine and Russia, from Myanmar to Darfur, from Iran to Lebanon, 250,000 people have lost their lives. Many more have endured indescribable suffering. Hundreds of thousands have been forced to leave the lands where they were born and raised. In Gaza alone, over the past three years,  74,000 of our brothers and sisters—most of them children and women—have fallen victim to Israel’s state terrorism. The people of Gaza are still searching for their loved ones beneath the rubble; they are uncovering the bodies of their spouses, children, mothers and fathers. Innocent children who have lost their arms and legs in Israeli attacks are trying to attend school and hold on to life with prosthetics made of wood. In hospitals in Gaza, more than 70 percent of generators are currently out of service due to fuel shortages.

As a father and a grandfather who cherishes his children and grandchildren dearly, I must state the following from this podium with my heart torn apart: Gaza today is not merely the world’s largest graveyard for children... It is also the territory with the highest rate of child amputees in the world. Gaza is the most inhumane and most shameful concentration camp of our time. Even after the ceasefire reached through the efforts of President Trump and the contributions of countries, including our own, the number of Gazans killed has exceeded 1,500. Although the Palestinian Resistance Movement has agreed to move to the second phase of the peace plan, the Israeli Government is unwilling to halt the occupation.

“UN, ESTABLISHED 81 YEARS AGO TO MAINTAIN PEACE AND SECURITY, HAS BECOME UNABLE TO FULFIL THIS MISSION”

Meanwhile, in the West Bank, we are witnessing the most severe period of settler terrorism. In Al-Quds, Muslims and Christians are being prevented from accessing their holy sites. There is an attempt to destroy UNRWA, a joint initiative of us all. Today, I will openly express certain realities here, without placing any barrier between my heart and my words: Let no one take offense, nor feel slighted or resented. This is not Tayyip Erdoğan’s personal issue... This is a humanitarian issue; it is a matter of conscience for us all. Before us stands a genocidal mentality that can never get enough of killing. Before us stands an extremely dire situation. No one who holds humanity, compassion and mercy in their heart, with a sense of justice and conscience, can turn a blind eye to this reality.

This scene, which ought to shake us all to the core, tells us this: The United Nations, established 81 years ago to maintain peace and security, has become unable to fulfil this mission, or rather it has been made unable to do so. The Organization continues to lose blood. Those who have placed their hopes in the United Nations in Palestine, Lebanon, Sudan and other crisis areas are deeply disappointed. But I would like to remind you that one day, everyone will have to seek refuge in humanity’s collective conscience. Today, we may feel safe, prosperous and at peace. We may live in comfort, far away from conflict zones and crisis areas. But none of us knows what tomorrow will bring or what might happen to us. That is why I find this year’s General Assembly theme, which focuses on restoring confidence in the international system, exceptionally accurate.

We support the sincere efforts of the Secretary-General in this direction, including the UN80 Initiative. We expect this commitment for reform to be maintained during the tenure of the next Secretary-General. Of course, I would also like to state a fundamental truth quite clearly here... If we genuinely wish to boost confidence in the United Nations, the necessary steps are evident: Children in Gaza must be safe. When Palestinian children look up at the sky, they will see kites soaring freely, not fighter jets, UAVs or drones. Children in Lebanon will not wake up in the middle of the night to the sound of bombs. The labor of Asian workers will not be exploited by ruthless capitalists. Our African brothers and sisters will feel just as safe and full of hope for their future as the citizens of prosperous countries. Only in this way, trust in the United Nations can be restored. Let’s recognize that a system in which the will of more than 190 countries is subject to the whims of five countries is neither fair nor capable of fully establishing trust. The Security Council must absolutely be reformed in accordance with the principle that ‘the world is bigger than five.’

“AN INTERNATIONAL SYSTEM WHERE IMPUNITY HAS BECOME THE NORM IS DOOMED TO DECAY”

While we must keep pace with rapidly advancing technology, we also bear the arduous yet noble responsibility of building a fairer order. At this point, I want to share with you here some basic principles: First and foremost, we are compelled to change the current understanding where international law is applied differently to the strong and the weak. Let us not forget that an international system where wrongdoers get away with it and, worse still, where impunity has become the norm, is doomed to decay. Second; at every stage where the international will is obstructed in resolving crises, we must use regional ownership to open a new path. As Türkiye, in every instance, such as the Black Sea Grain Corridor, where we have acted upon this principle, we have achieved result; we contributed both regional and global security. Third; we must absolutely reestablish an approach that places cooperation and open diplomacy at the center of relations among states. History has shown us, through bitter experiences, that there is no winner in a political approach built upon mistrust. Fourth; we must jointly build a new paradigm that offers solutions to the increasingly deepening income inequalities around the world. We believe that the path to this lies in joint development, solidarity and connectivity. Societies connected to one another through roads, trade, energy networks and joint production will eventually be united in peace and stability as well. Finally, by reasserting a human-centered understanding of technology, we must prevent new barriers to be erected between those who possess technology and those who do not. It must be understood that techno-polarization and digital hegemony serve neither the interests of the United Nations-centered system nor those of the states that constitute its core.

“ATTEMPTS TO STRANGLE THE STATE OF PALESTINE WILL FAIL”

As Türkiye, we do not confine ourselves with merely articulating these principles. With every step we take, we seek a fairer and more humane international system. Through the Defense Alliance we have established with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, based on the understanding of regional ownership, we are both strengthening solidarity among us and aiming to generate solutions to the problems in our region from within the region itself. We are maintaining our efforts with the relevant actors to bring an end to the climate of conflict and war that has been ignited in the Gulf. I strongly underline that dangerous attempt such as spreading these conflicts to neighboring regions serves no one’s interests.

As for Gaza, we remain determined to uphold our commitments we made in Sharm el-Sheikh one year ago. We must begin the reconstruction of Gaza without delay. In this regard, I call upon you to exert greater pressure on Israel. Let everyone now understand and accept this: Attempts to strangle the State of Palestine will fail. Allah willing, we shall see those auspicious days where an independent State of Palestine, based on the 1967 borders, with territorial integrity and East Al-Quds as its capital, is established.

“WE WILL CONTINUE TO STAND BY THE BROTHERLY SYRIAN PEOPLE”

After 14 years of oppression, Syria embarked on a new path with the December 8 Revolution. Under the leadership of President Sharaa, we are witnessing that Syria is moving toward its goal of becoming a safe and peaceful country, despite all forms of internal and external provocation. We will continue to stand by the brotherly Syrian people on this journey. In Iraq, another neighboring country, we fully support the efforts to strengthen the state authority and consolidate stability. We are working with Iraq on strategic transportation and energy projects that will enhance the welfare of our region, particularly the Development Road Project.

As for the Russia-Ukraine war, it is our sincere hope that it comes to an end with Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity being upheld. We continue our contacts with the parties with a view to restoring safety of navigation in the Black Sea, ensuring food security, and preventing the war from spreading to a wider geography. I would like to particularly emphasize that recent attacks against commercial vessels in the Black Sea, regardless of who carries them out, are unacceptable. We believe that freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz must be maintained.

I call upon the international community to recognize and establish political, diplomatic, and economic relations with the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.

Türkiye, thanks to its growing defence industry, and its resilient economy, continues to be an island of stability amid conflicts in its vicinity. As an integral part of Europe, our country plays a significant role in ensuring the welfare and security of the continent. The NATO Ankara Summit, which we successfully hosted in July, was a concrete manifestation of our commitment to our common security. A Europe that the

“WE WILL HOST COP31 SUMMIT IN ANTALYA IN NOVEMBER”

We all derive our livelihood and the source of our life from the nature. Yet our world stands on the threshold of serious environmental and climate-related threats. Air, water and soil, as well as many living species, are being affected by the climate change. While developing countries and the Pacific region are experiencing the climate crisis to their very core, they unfortunately face serious difficulties in accessing the funding they need. This November, we will host COP31 Summit in Antalya. At the Summit, we will ensure that climate justice is given particular prominence. Through the partnership we have developed with Australia, we aim to make COP31 an “Implementation COP,” where financial commitments are fulfilled, technology transfer is accelerated, and promises are translated into concrete steps. Taking this opportunity, I invite you to the COP31 Leaders’ Summit.

The Zero Waste Movement launched by my wife, Mrs. Emine Erdoğan, in 2017 with the slogan “The World is Our Common Home” has since evolved into a global campaign to raise awareness. It is a fact that there are undoubtedly many ways to tackle the climate crisis. The Zero Waste Movement is the strongest bridge where all these paths meet. I believe that, with your support, this bridge will become even stronger.

I would also like to draw your attention to the following fact: Another threat as serious as climate change is the spread of a culture of waste fueled by the desire for consumption. Every year, 5.8 trillion plates of food end up in the bin worldwide, meaning that over 2 billion tons of food are wasted. We cannot speak of justice in a world where tons of food are thrown into the garbage on one side while hundreds of millions of people collect food from garbage on the other. As Türkiye, we are ready to make every possible contribution both to preventing waste and to ensuring global food security. With this understanding, we nominated Dr. Mehmet Mehdi Eker for the position of Director-General of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. I am confident that you will not withhold your support.

“XENOPHOBIA, CULTURAL RACISM AND ANTI-SEMITISM ARE TOXIC TRENDS THAT MUST BE COMBATED WITH DETERMINATION”

It is also worth noting that: As our world changes rapidly, humanity has simultaneously begun to face new social threats. Islamophobia, which is spreading like the plague in the West, is at the forefront of these issues. Most of all, Muslim women and girls are subjected to greater discrimination in recent years. We regard the headscarf bans introduced in schools by certain countries as an attack on women’s most fundamental rights. Rising xenophobia, cultural racism and anti-Semitism are also toxic trends that must be combated with determination. Global gender-neutralization policies as well have turned into a siege targeting innocent children, alongside the family institution. We can break this siege only by protecting the family consisting of women and men. Türkiye will continue to take initiatives in protecting families and children, despite attacks from lobby groups.

“WE WILL NOT REMAIN SILENT IN THE FACE OF INJUSTICE”

The realities I have spoken of here today with an open heart will undoubtedly upset some people, disrupt their comfort, and unmask their lies. I also know very well that they will resort to all kinds of perception management operations in an attempt to silence our voice. In the words of a late poet: ‘They think that if we remain silent, the issue will disappear/But even if we remain silent, history will not./History may remain silent, but the truth will not./They believe that if they get rid of us, the problem will be solved./Yet even if they get rid of us, they would not be able to escape the pangs of their conscience./Even if they were to escape the pangs of their conscience,/They would not be able to escape the pangs of history,/Even if they were to escape the pangs of history,/They would not be able to escape the wrath of Allah.”

As Tayyip Erdoğan, as the President of a great nation guided by its conscience, its history and its compassion, Allah willing, for as long as Allah grants me life, I shall continue from this rostrum to defend the rights of the oppressed, the aggrieved and the voiceless; to be their voice; to speak on their behalf; and to fight for them. If necessary, we will endure hardship; if necessary, we will pay the price. But we will not remain silent in the face of injustice, and we will never consent to oppression.

When we look at the course of the world, we can see that there are two paths before us: Either we will deepen uncertainty through fear, conflict and isolation... Or we will build the future together through justice, solidarity and common will. It is, of course, easy to punch the darkness. The difficult thing is to light a candle that will dispel that darkness. Türkiye has chosen the second path and hopefully will follow it with patience. May Allah ease our way and be our guide and helper, I pray. I invite our friends listening to us in this hall and from every corner of the world to embrace this shared vision of the future. Until we meet again, I salute you all once more with respect.”

6. Global Peace and Security

Global peace and security are vital for sustainable socio-economic  development.  The  United  Nations,  through  its Charter,  has  remained  central  to  international  efforts  to maintain peace and security, uphold international law, and promote conditions conducive to development.

However,  despite  these  longstanding  commitments,  the persistence  of  armed  conflicts  around  the  world  reflects the  departure  from  the  purposes  and  principles  of  the Charter. This Monday, on my way to New York, somewhere in the sky over the big and beautiful Atlantic Ocean, I read President Trump’s post on Truth Social. The President wrote that “Russia has lost control of its diesel oil industry due to its war with Ukraine…”

And it is hard to imagine a more humiliating loss for a country that has a permanent seat on the UN Security Council and takes so much pride in its oil exports.

I quote: “A large number of their diesel refineries have been blown up and are, at least temporarily, out of commission.” End of quote.

And this is true. Russia messed up.

And the conclusion of the post is also right: “…this ridiculous and never-ending war with Ukraine must be ended…”

I do not know a single world leader who would say otherwise. I do not know anyone who is openly for this war…

Except one man.

For almost five years now, Russian generals have been trying to carry out Putin’s crazy order to seize our eastern land – the Donetsk region.

And just this year, from January through August, the Russian army lost 248,964 people on the battlefield in Ukraine. In 8 months. 248 thousand. Killed and badly wounded. Twenty-one countries in the world have smaller populations than the number of Russian troops lost in just these 8 months.

We have video confirmation for every one of these losses. And these are not just statistics. It’s about people. We have an archive of drone videos – videos showing thousands and thousands of Russians losing their lives in kill zones…

It is madness. But they still keep going there to die. Because that is what Putin wants.

After losing so many people, Russia managed to capture just over one thousand square kilometers of our land this year – and we have already liberated a significant part of it.

Russia is a country that already has 17 million square kilometers of its own land – without any Ukrainian territory, by the way. So to add another thousand square kilometers, Putin is paying with 248 people for every kilometer…

Does anyone still think that he is reasonable and moderate?
